description: Every caveat a look-alike call writes itself, in the order both SDKs emit them: the response's degradation; then `application_filter` (a baseline filter replaced the model's `employee_count.gte`); `anchors_unreported`, `anchors_by_name` and `anchors_zero_weight`; `limit_capped` (the model asked for 5 rows, the application returns at most 2); `anchors_removed` (the domain anchor came back as its own look-alike); and last `rows_without_lookup`.

degradation.detail: 9% of company records have no embedding and were matched lexically only.

caveats: vector_coverage_incomplete: 9% of company records have no embedding and were matched lexically only. (impact: recall)
application_filter: `filters.employee_count.gte` is fixed by this application to 500; your 100 was not applied.
anchors_unreported: the API does not report which of the 3 anchors resolved. Say the results are based on the anchors provided, not that they match every one.
anchors_by_name: Adyen — resolved by name with no disambiguation, so a same-named company may have been used. Prefer a domain.
anchors_zero_weight: checkout.com — weight 0, so no influence on the result.
limit_capped: you asked for 5 rows; this application returns at most 2 per call.
anchors_removed: stripe.com — returned as a look-alike of itself and removed.
rows_without_lookup: 1 of 2 rows carry no domain or LinkedIn URL, so they have no `lookup` value and cannot be looked up.
